title: Humiliating legal defeat for Bachelorette 'sleaze' who told Angie Kent he'd 'slip the tongue in': Tribunal rejects former Noosa councillor's excuses after five-year fight
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Humiliating legal defeat for Bachelorette 'sleaze' who told Angie Kent he'd 'slip the tongue in': Tribunal rejects former Noosa councillor's excuses after five-year fight

He became one of The Bachelorette's most notorious contestants after telling Angie Kent he'd 'slip the tongue in'. Now his long-running legal fight has ended in a humiliating defeat.

Actual Article Body:
By MADELEINE DAMO - WEALTH AND WORKPLACE REPORTER

Published:  00:00 AEST, 7 October 2026   |  Updated:  16:58 AEST, 7 October 2026

A former Noosa councillor who was booted off The Bachelorette for lewd on-screen behaviour has failed in his attempt to reduce the fine imposed on him seven years after his infamous appearance.

Jess Glasgow took annual leave from Noosa Shire Council to join the fifth season of The Bachelorette in 2019, starring Angie Kent.

His tenure lasted just two episodes before Ms Kent asked him to leave, citing multiple instances of inappropriate conduct.

The brief stint sparked 128 complaints to the local government regulator and a subsequent investigation. Despite public calls for his resignation, Mr Glasgow remained on council until he was voted out in May 2020.

In February 2021, the Councillor Conduct Tribunal found him guilty of misconduct relating both to his behaviour on-screen and to his media appearances afterwards.

Mr Glasgow was ordered to pay Noosa Shire Council $4,000 (15 penalty units) and $1,000 in costs.

Both episodes were screened in full for the Tribunal, including a scene where Mr Glasgow bragged about kissing women without permission, saying: 'I've kissed plenty of girls and they've turned their heads before. I'm used to it.'

That comment came as cast members watched a photo shoot between Ms Kent and another contestant, speculating about whether the pair would share a kiss.

Jess Glasgow took annual leave from Noosa Shire Council to appear on the fifth season of the Bachelorette which aired in 2019, starring Angie Kent

His tenure lasted just two episodes before he was kicked off by Ms Kent following several instances of inappropriate behaviour

At the end of the second episode, Mr Glasgow was ordered to pack his bags, with Bachelorette Angie Kent fed up with him viewing her as a 'piece of meat'

Mr Glasgow also quipped: 'If it was me, I would've laid one on her; just slip the tongue in' and, 'S***, I bet she's turned on, she's up for it'.

The peak of Mr Glasgow's antics came during a separate photo shoot, when Ms Kent was told to climb onto his back as he played the role of a horse.

He told Ms Kent, 'Don't mind me if I get some wandering fingers, alright,' then declared to the camera, 'I'm gonna be the first person she's gonna get to ride.'

Viewers saw Mr Glasgow urge Ms Kent to 'come on, pat the horse's bum', prompting a male co-star to tell him, 'Stop being a sleaze, bro.'

He was also shown making lewd gestures with his mouth towards Ms Kent's bottom, and exclaiming, 'Damn, this beats my last girlfriend.'

One cast member told Ms Kent that even members of the production team had been made deeply uncomfortable by his behaviour.

At the end of the second episode, Ms Kent asked Mr Glasgow to leave, saying she was fed up with being treated as a 'piece of meat'.

Mr Glasgow told the Sunshine Coast Daily his appearance on the show was a 'once in a lifetime opportunity' and a great conversation starter at a summer barbecue

While leaving The Bachelorette mansion, Mr Glasgow told viewers his behaviour was 'just harmless fun' and that he'd return to Noosa to find the love of his life 'in a dirty, dingy nightclub'.

Soon after, he told the Sunshine Coast Daily his appearance was a 'once in a lifetime opportunity' and the perfect conversation starter at a summer barbecue.

Mr Glasgow also claimed he had the blessing of Noosa's then mayor, Tony Wellington, quoting him as saying, 'What I do on annual leave is up to me, just don't bring council into disrepute.'

He made similar claims on ABC Radio, but a response from Mayor Wellington clarified Glasgow had not sought approval for his appearance.

At the February 2021 hearing, the Tribunal was told Mr Glasgow had 'behaved in an inappropriate way, making offensive comments and gestures' towards Ms Kent, as well
